candidate_review.conclusion: Existing distant-task candidate/exact-open oracle is the closest value asset; extend it with a typed public Host lane, 100k events, cache rebuild, cold restart, authority-state invariance, and bounded ResumePackage checks.
Existing immutable binding/effect-authority oracle remains valid; extend it with wrong-principal search, candidate-only non-mutation, single foreground Run rejection, and durable Auto snapshot facts.
Its natural-language five-way routing is S5/S6 scope. Record an explicit non-gating S4 boundary and do not duplicate the required search/open assertions already carried by TC-HM-02.
Existing one-foreground-Run/FIFO oracle is reusable after isolating a deterministic Host lane from S5 Context/closure/provider assertions and adding duplicate/lost-ACK/restart boundaries.
Existing six-view steps are reusable after adding a graph-independent public Host lane for 1k/10k/100k limits, stable paging, byte-identical rebuild, drift, and projection fault replay.

decisions.reason: TC-HM-02 proves 100k candidate-to-exact-open bounded recovery, while the non-overlapping TC-HM-11 Host lane proves queued-turn continuity in the same value journey.
The existing six-view oracle is retained, but its required S4 lane is made graph/UI independent and adds exact size, page, rebuild, drift, and replay expectations.
The existing foreground Run case already owns FIFO/control semantics; the extension separates deterministic Host behavior from out-of-scope Context and provider behavior.

None of the reviewed cases covers fresh Host composition, the single writable primary, legacy/future epoch rejection, old Session CRUD fences, and emergency export through public APIs. One minimal scripted case groups these coupled Host-closure behaviors without adding UI or model routing.

The reviewed cases contain rebuild or restart checks but no public raw-manifest invariant spanning CRUD rejection, ingress fence, drain-or-park, WAL checkpoint, replay, and export. TC-HM-14 adds that single missing Host recovery oracle.

TC-HM-02 owns permission-first candidate/exact-open behavior; TC-HM-09 adds the distinct binding/Run authority invariant. TC-HM-10 is not selected because its S4-relevant search/open portion would duplicate TC-HM-02 and its remaining route behavior is out of scope.

The existing cases are feature or UI journeys and do not define one-per-entrypoint critical plus affected public API smoke for the new Host composition. TC-HM-14 adds only that missing scripted surface and leaves full pytest, static checks, and execution evidence to the verification run.
